item.research_question: Whether it is necessary to use all five elements (Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, Zr) to achieve a random solid solution and good mechanical properties, or if reducing the system to 3 or 4 elements yields similar results.
item.material_system: HfNbTaTiZr system; specific alloys: HfNbTaTiZr (5-element), NbTaTiZr, NbTaTi, NbTiZr, TaTiZr, Nb0.5TaTiZr1.5, Nb1.5TaTiZr0.5 (3 and 4-element MEAs).
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc melting in a water-cooled copper crucible; elements with 99.9% purity; ingots cast 8 times and flipped for mixing; no Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) or heat treatment applied to cast material.
item.test_conditions: Room temperature tensile testing with a strain rate of 2 × 10−4 s−1; Vickers hardness HV30 measurements; microstructure and phase analysis via SEM, WDS, and XRD.
key_findings: The 5-element HfNbTaTiZr alloy exhibits the best combination of strength and elongation among all studied alloys.
The 4-element NbTaTiZr alloy has similar strength to the 5-element alloy but reduced elongation to 6.4%.
The TaTiZr alloy exhibited brittle behavior, breaking before reaching the yield point.
The NbTaTi alloy showed the highest elongation and the lowest hardness of 246 HV.
Simultaneous presence of Ta and Zr resulted in a significant reduction of ductility due to a reduction in BCC1 phase content.
Precipitation of Ta-rich particles on grain boundaries reduced maximum elongation to failure to zero values in brittle alloys.
A clear linear relationship exists between total elongation and the BCC1 phase content.
Grain size was estimated around 0.5 mm for all alloys except NbTiZr, which showed no dendritic segregation.
item.mechanism: The simultaneous presence of Ta and Zr causes segregation during solidification due to a miscibility gap in the Ta-Zr binary phase diagram, leading to the formation of two BCC phases (BCC1 and BCC2) and intergranular Ta-rich precipitates. The reduction in the BCC1 phase content and the presence of these precipitates on grain boundaries are responsible for the significant reduction in ductility and the transition to brittle fracture.
item.limitations: The study did not investigate the BCC2 and BCC3 phases or intergranular precipitates in detail. The relation between hardness and the misfit parameter δ is complicated because not all alloys are single-phase. The role of rapid cooling versus chemical composition in phase stability requires further verification.
item.future_work: Further research shall focus on detailed investigations of the BCC2 and BCC3 phases and intergranular precipitates. The destabilizing effect of Ta + Zr on BCC phase stability during manufacturing and aging shall be verified. The stabilizing effect of Hf on HCP phase formation during mid-temperature aging and the influence of cooling rate on phase composition shall be investigated.
quotes: Simultaneous presence of Ta and Zr in the alloy resulted in a significant reduction of ductility caused by reduction of the BCC phase content.
Precipitation of Ta rich particles on grain boundaries reduces further the maximum elongation to failure down to zero values.
Clear correlation between the BCC1 phase content and the total elongation to failure of the alloy was found.
